title: Recursive Language Models
abstract: We study allowing large language models (LLMs) to process arbitrarily long prompts through the lens of inference-time scaling. We propose Recursive Language Models (RLMs), a general inference paradigm that treats long prompts as part of an external environment and allows the LLM to programmatically examine, decompose, and recursively call itself over snippets of the prompt.

key_insights.author: Alex Zhang
key_insights.quote: Much like the switch in 2025 from language models to reasoning models, we think 2026 will be all about the switch to Recursive Language Models (RLMs). It turns out that models can be far more powerful if you allow them to treat their own prompts as an object in an external environment.
key_insights.highlight: 2026 will be the year of RLMs

key_insights.author: Alex Zhang
key_insights.quote: On the OOLONG benchmark, RLMs with GPT-5-mini outperforms GPT-5 by over 110% gains (more than double!) on 132k-token sequences and is cheaper to query on average.

key_insights.author: Omar Khattab
key_insights.quote: Most people (mis)understand RLMs to be about LLMs invoking themselves. The deeper insight is LLMs interacting with their own prompts as objects.

key_insights.author: Omar Khattab
key_insights.quote: My favorite part of Alex's post is studying what the recursive LM actually decides to do—how does it take a variable with 10M tokens and figure it out? You see strategies like: peeking, map/reduce, summarization, and output accumulation.

core_concepts.title: Recursive Decomposition
core_concepts.simple_explanation: Instead of processing a huge prompt all at once, the model breaks it into smaller chunks and processes them recursively, like dividing a big task into sub-tasks.
core_concepts.technical_definition: A paradigm where the root LM (depth=0) can spawn isolated sub-RLM instances using transformed versions of the context with their own isolated environments. Each recursive call operates on a subset of the original context.
core_concepts.analogy: Like a manager delegating parts of a large project to team members, who can further delegate to their own teams if needed.
core_concepts.why_it_matters: Enables processing of contexts 100x beyond model context windows without degradation. Even within normal limits, improves accuracy by avoiding 'context rot'.
core_concepts.misconception: NOT just about LLMs calling themselves repeatedly. The key is treating prompts as manipulable objects in an external environment.

core_concepts.title: REPL Environment
core_concepts.simple_explanation: The model operates inside a Python notebook environment where the huge context is stored as a variable. The model writes code to inspect, slice, and process this variable.
core_concepts.technical_definition: A Python REPL (Read-Eval-Print Loop) Notebook environment similar to Jupyter that stores the user's prompt as a variable in memory. The root LM interacts by outputting code blocks and receives truncated output in its context.
core_concepts.analogy: Like having a massive dataset loaded in a Jupyter notebook. You write Python code to explore, filter, and analyze it without loading the entire dataset into your working memory.
core_concepts.why_it_matters: The context window of the root LM rarely gets clogged because it never directly sees the entire context. Its input context grows slowly as it strategically explores the data.
key_features: Output truncated and fed back to model
Final answer via FINAL() or FINAL_VAR() tags

core_concepts.title: Context Chunking
core_concepts.simple_explanation: The model intelligently decides how to split large contexts into manageable pieces, adapting its strategy based on the query and context structure.
core_concepts.technical_definition: Dynamic partitioning of context based on query requirements. The model adaptively chooses chunk sizes and strategies (peeking, grepping, mapping) at test time rather than using fixed preprocessing.
core_concepts.analogy: Like reading a massive book by first checking the table of contents, then jumping to relevant chapters, and only reading specific sections in detail.
core_concepts.why_it_matters: Unlike rigid retrieval systems, RLMs defer chunking decisions to the model, which can adapt based on the specific query and context structure.

core_concepts.title: Sub-Query Delegation
core_concepts.simple_explanation: The root LM can call smaller LMs (like GPT-5-mini) to answer specific sub-questions about parts of the context, then combine their answers.
core_concepts.technical_definition: The root LM (depth=0) can recursively call LMs (depth=1) inside its REPL environment. These recursive calls operate on transformed subsets of context and return results to the root environment.
core_concepts.analogy: A senior engineer breaking down a complex problem and assigning specific tasks to junior developers, then integrating their solutions.
core_concepts.why_it_matters: Recursive depth of 1 is sufficient for most tasks. Using smaller models (GPT-5-mini) for sub-queries makes the system cheaper while maintaining or exceeding frontier model performance.

code_examples.title: Basic RLM Usage
code_examples.description: Simple API call that feels like standard LLM usage
code_examples.code:
from rlm import RLM

# Initialize RLM with your preferred model
rlm = RLM(model="gpt-5-mini")

# Query with huge context - feels like a normal LLM call
response = rlm.completion(
    query="Summarize the key findings",
    context=ten_million_token_document
)

print(response)  # Returns summary

code_examples.title: Peeking Strategy
code_examples.description: Root LM inspects context structure before processing
code_examples.code:
# Root LM writes this code in REPL:
preview = context[:2000]
print(preview)

# Output (truncated) returns to LM:
# Date: Dec 12, 2022 || User: 63685 || Instance: How many...
# Date: Dec 30, 2024 || User: 35875 || Instance: What war...

# LM decides: 'I see a pattern - Date || User || Instance'
code_examples.simplified: preview = context[:2000]  # LM peeks at structure

code_examples.title: Grepping Strategy
code_examples.description: Search for specific patterns to narrow context
code_examples.code:
import re

# Root LM searches for specific user IDs
user_ids = ['67144', '53321', '38876']
pattern = r'User: (' + '|'.join(user_ids) + r')'

# Find matching lines
matches = [line for line in context.split('\n') 
           if re.search(pattern, line)]

# Now recursively process only matching lines
for chunk in chunk_list(matches, 10):
    result = recursive_lm("Label these questions", chunk)

code_examples.title: Partition + Map
code_examples.description: Split context and process chunks in parallel
code_examples.code:
# Split 10M tokens into 100 chunks of 100k each
chunk_size = 100000
chunks = [context[i:i+chunk_size] 
          for i in range(0, len(context), chunk_size)]

# Map: Process each chunk with recursive LM
results = []
for i, chunk in enumerate(chunks[:10]):  # First 10 chunks
    result = recursive_lm(
        f"Label questions in chunk {i}",
        chunk
    )
    results.append(result)

# Reduce: Combine results
final_answer = combine_results(results)

code_examples.title: FINAL Answer
code_examples.description: Root LM signals completion with FINAL tag
code_examples.code:
# Root LM can output directly:
FINAL("The answer is 42.")

# Or use a variable from REPL:
final_answer = compute_answer(processed_context)
FINAL_VAR(final_answer)

# RLM extracts answer and returns to user
